criteria.criterion: In crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, the `queue` subject uses `crate::plan::title_line(&request.text)` (then the 60-char cap) instead of `lines().next()`; check the diff.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. `queue` now calls `queue_subject(&request.text)`. The new `queue_subject` helper (reading.rs:1358) does `crate::plan::title_line(text).chars().take(60).collect()` and formats it as `Queue a request: {line}`. The old `request.text.lines().next()...take(60)` code is gone.

criteria.criterion: A new test in reading.rs queues a request whose first line is 'Priority: urgent' followed by a real request line. It asserts the commit subject is 'Queue a request: <real line>' and does not contain 'Priority'. Check with `cargo test -p athena-core` and the test name in the diff.
criteria.evidence: `a_queued_request_commit_names_the_request_not_its_priority` calls `athena.queue("Priority: urgent\n\nFix the widget")` on a temporary git repo. It reads the real subject back with `git log -1 --format=%s`, asserts it equals `Queue a request: Fix the widget`, and asserts it does not contain `Priority`. A second unit test checks `queue_subject` directly, including the case where every line is a Priority line. Both passed when I ran them. On base, `queue` used the raw first line, so the subject would have been `Queue a request: Priority: urgent` and the commit test would fail.

criteria.criterion: The diff shows no raw first-line subject left for a Dropped commit. The Dropped subject path (manage.rs via `job.title()`) is either shown to use `title_line` or changed to use it.
criteria.evidence: I read the code; nothing needed to change. manage.rs:211 builds the closing subject with `crate::run::closing_subject(state, &job.title())`, and for OutcomeState::Dropped that gives `Dropped: <title>` (run/close.rs:640). store.rs:151-158 `JobRecords::title` uses `crate::plan::title_line(&req.text)` when the job has no reading. I searched for `lines().next()` and found no Dropped subject built from the raw first line. The CHANGELOG entry says the same.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry under the unreleased section saying that queued and dropped request commit subjects skip leading Priority lines.
criteria.evidence: CHANGELOG.md lines 25-29, under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed`, say that the commit subjects of queued and dropped requests skip leading `Priority:` lines and blank lines. The entry names `queue_subject` and explains why the Dropped code is unchanged.

criteria.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, and `cargo test` all pass, and the existing `title_line` tests in plan.rs still pass unchanged.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for 16d4f048 (CI run 42553186098) show fmt, clippy and test all passing. plan.rs is not in the diff, and `plan::tests::the_title_line_skips_priority_lines_and_blanks` passed when I ran it.

criteria.criterion: The diff touches only reading.rs, CHANGELOG.md, and plan.rs or manage.rs if needed; no other behavior changes.
criteria.evidence: The diff stat shows only CHANGELOG.md and crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. The only change outside the tests is how the queue subject is computed; the commit body and trailers are unchanged.

findings.summary: The new commit-level test sets up its git repository inline instead of using a shared fixture.
findings.evidence: `a_queued_request_commit_names_the_request_not_its_priority` repeats git init, config, writing athena.toml/defaults.toml and the bootstrap commit. That makes the tests module longer, but it is correct.

findings.summary: No new test covers the Dropped subject for a request that starts with a Priority line.
findings.evidence: The Dropped subject is right by construction: `closing_subject(state, &job.title())` gets its title from `title_line`. But the diff adds no test that closes a queued job and checks the `Dropped:` subject. The code is correct today; a future change to the close path could break this without any test failing.

summary: The change does what the request asked, and I recommend passing it. The "Queue a request:" commit subject is now taken from the existing `plan::title_line` helper, which skips leading Priority and blank lines; the 60-character cap stays. I confirmed by reading the code that the "Dropped:" subject already used the same helper through `job.title()` (manage.rs:211 and store.rs:151), so it needed no code change. The new test queues "Priority: urgent\n\nFix the widget" on a real git repo and reads the subject back as "Queue a request: Fix the widget". I ran it and it passed; on the base code it would fail. The existing `title_line` test in plan.rs also passed when I ran it. The CHANGELOG entry is under Unreleased/Fixed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks all passed. Only reading.rs and CHANGELOG.md changed, both on the deliverables list. My two findings are small: the new test sets up its repository inline (nit), and nothing tests the Dropped subject directly (minor).
